title: Parliament Question: Availability of Special Educators in Schools
body_text:
Education is a subject under the Concurrent List of the Constitution and the majority of schools are under the administrative control of the respective state governments and Union Territory (UT) administrations. The Department of School Education & Literacy is implementing the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Samagra Shiksha to support States and UTs in providing equitable and inclusive quality education from pre-primary to Class XII.
Under the Samagra Shiksha framework, recruitment and other service matters relating to teachers, including Special Educators, fall within the domain of the respective State Governments/UT Administrations. The framework also provides for Special Educators to be deployed at the block or cluster level, as per requirement, and to work in an itinerant mode, covering a group of schools where Children with Special Needs (CwSN) are enrolled, so that their educational needs are adequately addressed.
Under Samagra Shiksha and PM SHRI (PM Schools for Rising India), financial assistance is provided to States and UTs for strengthening school education, including maintaining appropriate Pupil-Teacher Ratios (PTRs) and supporting inclusive education. This includes provision for two Resource Persons for CwSN at each Block Resource Centre (BRC).
The Department has notified the Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) for Special Educators in general schools for CwSN vide Notification No. S.O. 4586(E) dated 21.09.2022, published on 29.09.2022, as follows:
(i)  One Special Educator for every 10 CwSN at the primary level; and
(ii) One Special Educator for every 15 CwSN at the upper-primary level.
As per UDISE+ 2025–26, 1.17 lakh schools have a dedicated Special Educator. A statement indicating the State/UT-wise details of enrolment of CwSN and the number of schools having a dedicated Special Educator, as per UDISE+ 2025–26, is placed at Annexure.
The Department also supports capacity building of teachers and special educators through continuous professional development, in-service training, and awareness and sensitization programmes on inclusive education. National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) has developed online teacher training modules under National Initiative for School Heads' and Teachers' Holistic Advancement (NISHTHA) for the Elementary, Secondary and Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (FLN) stages, equipping general teachers to address the diverse learning needs of CwSN. NCERT and Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) have also developed handbooks on Inclusive Education to provide practical guidance to teachers for addressing the diverse needs of children in inclusive classrooms.
Further, the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE) has integrated two dedicated credits on Inclusive Education for CwSN in the Four-Year Integrated Teacher Education Programme (ITEP) for pre-service teacher education. This is aimed at equipping prospective teachers with the knowledge and skills required to ensure inclusion and meaningful participation of CwSN in regular schools and to adapt teaching-learning processes to address diverse learning needs, including those associated with learning disabilities.
The Rehabilitation Council of India (RCI), a statutory body of the Government of India responsible for regulating and monitoring the training of rehabilitation professionals and personnel, is mandated to develop human resources in 16 categories of rehabilitation professionals/personnel. RCI has granted approval to 1,081 institutions/universities to offer courses in disability rehabilitation and special education, thereby contributing to the availability of qualified human resources, including Special Educators.

enrichment.summary: In a Rajya Sabha written reply on 12 August 2026, the Ministry of Education stated that recruitment of teachers, including Special Educators, is a state subject, with the Centre supporting inclusive education through Samagra Shiksha and PM SHRI schemes. As per UDISE+ 2025-26 data, 22.11 lakh Children with Special Needs (CwSN) are enrolled nationally, but only about 1.17 lakh schools (of many more) have a dedicated Special Educator. The Department has notified a Pupil-Teacher Ratio for Special Educators (1:10 at primary, 1:15 at upper-primary level) and supports teacher capacity-building via NCERT, NCTE, CBSE and the Rehabilitation Council of India (RCI).
enrichment.context:
Inclusive education for Children with Special Needs (CwSN) has been a persistent policy challenge in India, given the vast gap between the number of children needing special educators and the actual availability of trained personnel, especially in rural and remote areas. Samagra Shiksha, launched in 2018 by merging earlier schemes like Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, RMSA and Teacher Education, is the umbrella Centrally Sponsored Scheme for school education from pre-primary to Class XII, with inclusive education as one of its key components. The Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 and the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 both emphasize inclusive and equitable education, mandating adequate special educators and accessible infrastructure, though implementation lags due to the states' primary role in teacher recruitment under the Concurrent List.

The notified PTR for Special Educators (1:10 primary, 1:15 upper-primary) issued in September 2022 was meant to standardize deployment, but the itinerant/cluster-based model reflects the practical shortage of qualified special educators, allowing one educator to serve multiple schools. The Rehabilitation Council of India (RCI), established under the RCI Act, 1992, plays a crucial regulatory role by accrediting institutions offering special education courses, directly affecting the supply pipeline of trained professionals. Efforts like NISHTHA training modules, ITEP credits on inclusive education, and NCERT/CBSE handbooks aim to mainstream disability-inclusive pedagogy among general teachers, given that dedicated special educators alone cannot meet the scale of need across 22 lakh+ CwSN.

prelims_questions.question: As per the Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) notified by the Department of School Education & Literacy for Special Educators, what is the prescribed ratio at the primary level?
options: One Special Educator for every 5 CwSN
One Special Educator for every 10 CwSN
One Special Educator for every 15 CwSN
One Special Educator for every 20 CwSN
prelims_questions.explanation: The notification S.O. 4586(E) dated 21.09.2022 prescribes one Special Educator for every 10 CwSN at the primary level and one for every 15 CwSN at the upper-primary level.

prelims_questions.question: Which statutory body is mandated to develop human resources across 16 categories of rehabilitation professionals, including Special Educators, in India?
options: National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT)
prelims_questions.explanation: The Rehabilitation Council of India (RCI), a statutory body under the RCI Act 1992, regulates and monitors training of rehabilitation professionals, including granting approval to institutions offering special education courses.

mains_questions.question: Education is a subject in the Concurrent List, yet school-level implementation, including recruitment of Special Educators, largely rests with States. Discuss the challenges this poses for ensuring inclusive education for Children with Special Needs (CwSN) and suggest measures to bridge the gap between enrolment and availability of trained educators.

Examine the role of Centrally Sponsored Schemes like Samagra Shiksha and PM SHRI in promoting inclusive education for differently-abled children in India. What structural and capacity-related challenges hinder their effective implementation?
